title: Army Rules, 1954 (India Code compilation) - r.23(3) caution sentence to the accused
issuer: Ministry of Defence (S.R.O. 484 of 27-11-1954), as compiled on India Code
pinpoint: PDF p.41, r.23(3) second sentence: 'Do you wish to make any statement? You are obliged to say anything unless you wish to do so, but whatever you say will be taken down in writing and may be given in evidence'; third sentence 'Any statement thereupon made by the accused shall be taken down and read over to him, but he will not be cross-examined upon it.'

title: The General Clauses Act, 1897 (Act 10 of 1897) - s.8 Construction of references to repealed enactments (India Code section record)
issuer: Parliament / Governor-General in Council (India Code consolidation, Legislative Department)
pinpoint: s.8(1): where any Central Act 'repeals and re-enacts, with or without modification, any provision of a former enactment, then references in any other enactment ... to the provision so repealed shall, unless a different intention appears, be construed as references to the provision so re-enacted.'
caveat: Text taken from the India Code section record metadata (JSON API response, hash of the saved response, not of a PDF). Whether s.8 applies to Army Act s.133's whole-Act reference to the Indian Evidence Act after BSA s.170 is a legal question not resolved; no judgment checked.
